logistics.title: The exception desk
logistics.text: This is the exception desk, a Selerim logistics concept built with fictional data. The problem is familiar: shipping documents arrive in different places, people match them by hand, and missing paperwork delays the next step. This guided tour uses captured states from the working application and synthetic narration. The current run uses deterministic PDF extraction and template drafts. It is not a live language model demonstration, and none of the names, shipments, or recipients represent real clients.

logistics.title: Document meets shipment record
logistics.text: The fixture contains fifty shipment records and forty documents. Here, shipment eight has a weight discrepancy. The document says three thousand two hundred fifteen pounds, while the shipment record says two thousand seven hundred fifteen. Both values appear together so a reviewer can understand the exception. The source panel shows extracted fields and links to the original PDF. The system uses exact shipment references within the job. Missing or unknown references go to review instead of being guessed.

logistics.title: Approval is a separate decision
logistics.text: The follow-up draft names the detected issue and asks for corrected or missing paperwork. A person reviews the evidence and chooses approve or reject. In this captured state, the reviewer has approved the draft, and a separate send action is now available. Approval does not itself send anything. That distinction is enforced by the server, not only by the appearance of a button. The acceptance tests also check that rejected drafts cannot be sent and changed evidence invalidates old approval.

logistics.title: A controlled transition
logistics.text: The reviewer then chooses send to demo outbox. The application records the state change and shows that the draft was sent to the local simulation. There is no SMTP connection and no external email API behind this action. All recipients use a non-deliverable domain. This deliberately narrow transport makes the concept safe to demonstrate while still exercising the actual approval and sending state machine. Repeating the same send does not create another outbox entry.

logistics.title: An inspectable outbox
logistics.text: The outbox preserves the approved recipient and message so the reviewer can inspect what the simulated action contained. This is fictional evidence, not a client result or a production integration. The system reads source records without changing them, limits file access to the current job, and logs its business actions. The model adapter, when separately configured, can help with wording. It has no approval or sending tool. This recorded run remains in the explicitly labeled template mode.

logistics.title: Measured on fictional fixtures
logistics.text: The activity log connects the source, draft, human decision, and simulated send. Its local hash chain is verifiable, although a database owner could defeat those controls. On the actual fixture parser run, all thirty clean documents matched correctly. All eleven planted document findings and sixty five missing-document gaps were detected, with no false positives. These are deterministic fixture results, not a promise about arbitrary scans or real operations. The next production step is a scoped audit of one workflow, its data, security requirements, and acceptance criteria.

legal.title: The matter room
legal.text: This is the matter room, a Selerim concept for preparing legal intake. It uses thirty fictional emails and their attachments, not client records. The task is to organize the materials, identify missing information, and give a human reviewer a factual brief with inspectable sources. This guided tour uses captured application states and synthetic narration. The current pipeline is deterministic. No live language model, real law firm inbox, or external messaging service is connected in this recording.

legal.title: Every claim has a source
legal.text: The brief appears beside the source material. Each factual statement has a citation naming its document, page, and line. Selecting the stated request highlights the exact line in the intake form. The reviewer can also switch to the engagement letter or open the original file. The paper surface is clearly labeled as extracted text. A requested review date is simply a fact supplied in the form; this tool does not calculate legal deadlines or offer legal advice.

legal.title: Incomplete matters stay visible
legal.text: The needs-information view separates matters that cannot pass the configured completeness checks. In this example, the company name in the engagement letter differs from the intake form. Other fixtures contain a missing engagement letter, an unsigned letter, or a missing contact email. The application flags the specific issue and offers a route to the local follow-up queue. It does not silently repair the documents, accept the client, or send a message. All twelve planted incomplete matters were routed correctly.

legal.title: The review gate
legal.text: For a complete intake, the reviewer checks the source materials and explicitly confirms that the brief has been reviewed. Approval then unlocks a separate action to file the reviewed intake. The application does not infer an attorney's decision from a document being present. This demonstration uses a local operator; it does not verify professional credentials. The server blocks approval for incomplete matters and blocks filing before approval. Changed source files also prevent the operation from completing under the old review.

legal.title: Filed does not mean accepted
legal.text: The filed view preserves the reviewed intake in the local demo. Filing does not establish an attorney-client relationship, clear a conflict, validate an engagement, or send any communication. The runtime retains selected fields, source citations, hashes, and review metadata rather than duplicating entire PDF and email bodies in the database. Original files remain in their matter folders. Access checks reject paths outside the matter and block documents that identify a different matter. Retention still requires an explicit operator policy.

legal.title: Evidence and limits
legal.text: The activity log makes source views and review decisions inspectable. The separate held-out evaluation contained ten fictional matters. The parser classified eighteen of eighteen documents correctly, extracted one hundred of one hundred fields, and produced fifty eight of fifty eight source-linked statements. Tests opened the cited files to verify the quoted lines. These numbers measure the generated text-PDF fixtures, not real-world legal accuracy, OCR, or model quality. The concept illustrates preparation with human oversight. A production engagement begins by defining the specific workflow, access boundaries, and measurable acceptance checks.
